c.tagline: Chile's UNESCO port city of cliffside funiculars, street art, and bohemian hills.

taxi.fareNote: Official radiotaxis run digital meters, while shared 'colectivos' (fixed-route taxis) charge a flat per-seat fare instead - confirm which type you're boarding before getting in.

emergency.note: 133 (Carabineros) is the most reliable general emergency line; 132 reaches the all-volunteer Bomberos fire service.

solo.f: daytime fine; extra caution at night

avoid.reason: Muggings on the cerros (hills) away from tourist routes and at night

hood_desc: The flat commercial core around Plaza Sotomayor and the port, home to government buildings, the naval headquarters, and the historic Mercado Puerto; best for first-timers who want the main squares and transit links within easy reach.

A hillside of colorful heritage houses, boutiques, and design shops reached by the Concepción and El Peral funiculars; suits travelers who want upscale cafes and shopping alongside classic Valparaíso views.
Valparaíso's oldest and most photographed hill, with cobbled Paseo Gervasoni, a Lutheran church, and panoramic lookouts over the bay; ideal for sightseers chasing the city's postcard views.
A bohemian, street-art-covered hill built around Pablo Neruda's La Sebastiana house; suits younger, artsy travelers drawn to murals and a more local, less polished atmosphere.
A quieter, largely residential hill west of the port near the university and the Punta Ángeles lighthouse; good for travelers wanting calm streets and sea views away from the tourist crowds.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though its mineral taste leads many to bottled.

transit.hours: Merval trains run roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; trolleybuses and local buses run similar hours with reduced late-night frequency.
transit.pay: Contactless transit cards are used on Merval trains and some buses, though many local buses and colectivos still take cash; the historic ascensores (funiculars) charge small separate cash fares.
transit.note: Valparaíso is famous for its historic ascensores (funiculars) linking the flat 'Plan' to the hillside cerros, and it retains one of the few operating trolleybus networks in the world.

air: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCL) in Santiago - no major airport in Valparaíso itself
bus: Turbus and Pullman Bus intercity coaches to Santiago and beyond
ferry: Port mainly serves cargo and cruise ships; no scheduled passenger ferry service

airport.name: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCL, Santiago)

transit.m: Airport shuttle/shared van to Valparaíso (~2 hours)

tip.r: A suggested 10% service charge ('sugerencia') is typically added as a separate line on restaurant bills; it isn't legally obligatory but most diners pay it, and it's not automatically included in the total.

food.name: Chorrillana
food.desc: A mountain of chips buried under sliced beef, fried onion and eggs, dumped in the middle of the table and attacked with forks. Invented here.

places.name: J. Cruz M. Malbran
places.note: The bar that claims to have invented chorrillana; chaotic, candlelit, covered in graffiti.

places.name: Bar La Playa
places.note: Century-old port bar with tiled floors, live music and a huge late-night chorrillana.

places.name: Bar Ingles
places.note: Historic wood-panelled bar near the port, good for a sit-down version.

food.name: Caldillo de congrio
food.desc: Neruda wrote an ode to it: conger eel poached with potato, onion, tomato and cream in a clay bowl, arriving still bubbling.

places.name: Bote Salvavidas
places.note: Classic harbourside seafood restaurant with boats moving past the windows.

places.name: Caleta Portales cocinerias
places.note: Upstairs kitchens above the working fishing cove; the fish landed that morning.

places.name: Cafe Turri
places.note: Grand old dining room with the best terrace view in the city and reliable seafood.

food.name: Empanadas de mariscos
food.desc: Baked or fried turnovers stuffed with prawn and cheese, machas, or crab, sold by the dozen from hole-in-the-wall counters all over the hills.

places.name: Delicias Express
places.note: Famous for oversized empanadas with dozens of fillings, open late.

places.name: Mercado Cardonal
places.note: Working produce market with cheap, excellent seafood empanadas at the food stalls.

places.name: Caleta Portales cocinerias
places.note: Fisherman's cove kitchens frying empanadas to order with the day's catch.

food.name: Chupe de jaiba
food.desc: Crab baked into a creamy bread-and-cheese casserole in an earthenware dish, browned on top. Rich enough to end the day right there.

places.name: Bote Salvavidas
places.note: Textbook chupe served in the traditional clay greda bowl.

places.name: Caleta Portales cocinerias
places.note: Unfussy versions made with crab landed metres away.

places.name: Cafe Turri
places.note: Refined take on the classic, worth it for the view alone.

food.name: Sopaipillas con pebre
food.desc: Pumpkin-dough discs fried on the street and topped with pebre salsa or sweet chancaca syrup. The default Valparaiso snack on a cold day.

places.name: Mercado Cardonal
places.note: Fried fresh at the market stalls and eaten standing at the counter.

places.name: Mercado Puerto
places.note: Restored heritage market hall with traditional Chilean snack counters.

places.name: Street carts, Plaza Anibal Pinto and Avenida Pedro Montt
places.note: Carts appear from mid-afternoon; look for the queue and the smell of frying.

food.name: Pescado frito with ensalada chilena
food.desc: Whole fried reineta or merluza with a simple salad of tomato, onion and coriander, plus a lemon wedge. Lunch as the port has eaten it forever.

places.name: Caleta Portales cocinerias
places.note: Pick your fish downstairs at the market, eat it fried upstairs.

places.name: Mercado Puerto
places.note: Market cookhouses doing cheap, fast fried fish plates at lunchtime.

places.name: Bote Salvavidas
places.note: A more formal version, right on the water at the passenger pier.

food.name: Pisco sour
food.desc: Chilean pisco shaken with lime, sugar and ice. Ordered before dinner in every hill bar; the terremoto wine cocktail is the rowdier cousin.

places.name: Bar Cinzano
places.note: Open since 1896; old waiters, boleros sung live, and a proper pisco sour.

places.name: Bar La Playa
places.note: Historic port bar, packed and loud after dark.

places.name: Fauna
places.note: Terrace bar with the classic postcard view over the bay at sunset.

food.name: Casablanca Valley white wine
food.desc: Cool-coast sauvignon blanc and chardonnay grown in the valley just inland, poured by the glass all over the hills. Borgona is the sweet local alternative.

places.name: Cafe Turri
places.note: Long Chilean list and a terrace looking straight down onto the port.

places.name: Fauna
places.note: Good coastal-valley whites to match the view and the seafood.

places.name: Bar Ingles
places.note: Old-school bar near the port for a quiet glass away from the crowds.

landmarks: Cerro Concepción and Cerro Alegre
Valparaíso's most beguiling hills, a UNESCO-listed labyrinth of candy-coloured mansions, boutique cafés and world-class street art tumbling toward the Pacific.
Ascensor Concepción and the Historic Funiculars
Creaking Victorian-era funicular elevators, the oldest running since 1883, haul passengers up impossibly steep hillsides and are the city's living icons.
La Sebastiana (Pablo Neruda's House)
The poet's whimsical five-storey ship-like home on Cerro Bellavista, packed with curios and offering intoxicating views over the harbour he adored.
Plaza Sotomayor and Monument to the Heroes of Iquique
The city's grand civic square, flanked by the palatial navy headquarters and a solemn crypt-monument honouring Arturo Prat and his naval heroes.
Paseo 21 de Mayo (Cerro Artillería)
A classic promenade viewpoint above the port, where sweeping panoramas take in cranes, container ships and the amphitheatre of painted hills.
Museo a Cielo Abierto (Open-Air Museum)
A hillside trail on Cerro Bellavista lined with twenty monumental murals created in the 1990s by Chile's greatest artists, including Matta and Nemesio Antúnez.
Palacio Baburizza (Museo de Bellas Artes)
An Art Nouveau palace on Paseo Yugoslavo housing Valparaíso's fine-arts museum, its turrets and terraces as captivating as the paintings within.
Muelle Prat and the Harbour Boat Tours
The bustling passenger pier where lanchas depart for cheap harbour cruises past navy frigates, sea lions and the best skyline view of the hills.
Iglesia La Matriz
The port's oldest church, a whitewashed 1837 landmark at the foot of Cerro Santo Domingo, marking the historic birthplace of Valparaíso.
Ascensor Artillería
The most scenic of all the funiculars, rattling up from the port to Paseo 21 de Mayo with the city's postcard panorama unfolding behind you.

train.note: No international trains - Chile's only cross-border passenger rail is the Arica-Tacna line to Peru, 2,000 km north. Merval's suburban trains run along the coast from Valparaíso to Viña del Mar in 10 minutes and inland to Limache, but there is no through service to Santiago; the old Santiago line closed to passengers. Take the bus for Santiago.

intl.to: Mendoza (Argentina) - over the Los Libertadores pass, ~9 hr

bus.note: The Mendoza coaches climb the Los Libertadores pass past Aconcagua - a spectacular ride that closes in winter storms, sometimes for days, so check conditions and carry your passport. Domestic buses from the Rodoviário terminal run to Santiago every few minutes on Turbus (https://www.turbus.cl/) and Pullman, taking about 90 minutes.

ferry.note: Valparaíso is Chile's historic main port but handles containers and cruise calls rather than scheduled passenger ferries. Short harbour tours run from Muelle Prat. Chile's real ferry network - Navimag through the fjords and the Chiloé crossings - operates far to the south from Puerto Montt.

half.name: Vina del Mar
half.blurb: Vina del Mar is a beach resort city next to Valparaiso, with a flower clock, casino and long sandy waterfront.

half.name: Casablanca Valley
half.blurb: Casablanca Valley is a wine region between Valparaiso and Santiago known for cool-climate Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay.

half.name: Isla Negra
half.blurb: Isla Negra is a coastal village south of Valparaiso where poet Pablo Neruda kept a ship-themed house filled with collected curios.

half.name: Concon
half.blurb: Concon is a beach town north of Valparaiso known for sand dunes, seafood restaurants and a pelican-lined fishing cove.
